STEP 1 - Scene: A snack of almonds on a small paper plate, photographed from directly overhead (top-down).

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a paper plate, likely a side/dessert plate of ~18 cm diameter. It spans about 260 px in the image. Area = 3.14 x 9^2 ≈ 254 cm^2. That gives ~0.069 cm per px, so ~14 px per cm.

STEP 3 - Items: Whole almonds (appear to be raw or unblanched, in skin). No sauce or oil is visible.

STEP 4 - Area: There are about 24 almonds. Each is roughly 45 px long and 25 px wide, which is about 3.2 cm x 1.8 cm. That is larger than a typical almond (~2.3 cm x 1.3 cm), but the plate scale suggests this size, so I will use ~2.6 x 1.5 cm. Each covers about 3 cm^2, so 24 almonds ≈ 72 cm^2, or about 28% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: Almonds are about 1 cm thick, so 72 cm^2 x 1 cm = 72 ml gross. (Check by piece: each ~1.2 g with 24 pieces ≈ 29 g; the volume approach is below.)

STEP 6 - Grams: Bulk density for whole almonds with gaps is about 0.6 g/ml, so 72 x 0.6 ≈ 43 g. Per piece this is ~1.8 g, which fits the larger size. I will take ~35 g as a compromise between the two methods.

STEP 7 - Energy: Almonds are about 580 kcal/100 g, so 35 g ≈ 203 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 24 almonds is roughly 30–35 g, which is a small handful and plausible for this plate.
